title: Establish Ubiquitous Language as the first Language Project example
outcome: Produce one reviewable, context-bounded Ubiquitous Language example and its recurring maintenance discipline, then use the Governance Policy exercise to show how one business expression is mapped into CyberAlchemy and DomainSpec vocabulary without silently redefining either source.
rationale: A language model becomes useful only when it can preserve one meaning across conversation, definitions, formal models, implementation, and evidence while making ambiguity and owner decisions visible.
scope: candidate definitions of Language and Ubiquitous Language
a distinct Ubiquitous Language Practice discipline candidate
the in-progress Governance Policy concept-resolution exercise
a typed ontology view and deterministic package validation
exclusions: canonical promotion of Language or Ubiquitous Language
claim that one vocabulary applies unchanged to every bounded context
settling the active Governance Policy classification before its owner review
automatic mutation of FormalClaims, DomainSpec definitions, or implementation
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus the owner of the Governance bounded-context language

success_conditions.statement: Language and Ubiquitous Language have separate candidate meanings with formal, plain-language, domain-context, and boundary voices.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Validated concept records with stable candidate IDs and no canonical authority claim.

success_conditions.statement: The Ubiquitous Language Practice is modeled separately from the language it maintains.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A discipline candidate that instantiates CAV2-D50 and explicitly cannot define or promote terms.

success_conditions.statement: Define and Definition Pack can consume the language model through explicit concept dispositions and owner routes.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Typed ontology links and an exercised Definition Pack mapping with all references resolved.

success_conditions.statement: The Governance Policy exercise reaches an owner-reviewed mapping across business meaning, CyberAlchemy vocabulary, and DomainSpec meta-types.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A completed exercise record with accepted dispositions, exact source bindings, and owner decision references.

success_conditions.statement: A downstream FormalClaim and implementation can reference the same concept identities without copying definition authority into either artifact.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: One admitted definition-closure graph and one implementation mapping that preserve the accepted concept IDs and exact source bindings.

evidence_requirements: Evidence must identify exact sources, context, owner, observed result, and claim limit.
Structural package validation cannot promote a concept, admit a discipline, accept a Definition Pack, or achieve this Goal.
Achievement requires all success conditions to be met and a separate owner-recorded lifecycle decision.

evidence_refs.claim_limit: Supports only the candidate package shape and explicit integration links; it does not support canonical meaning or successful use.

current_condition: candidate-model-created; first concept-resolution exercise remains in progress

revision_history.change: Created the Language Project, Language Project Space, and Ubiquitous Language first-example goal as candidate, effect-free artifacts.

challenge_route: Challenge the language meanings through definitions-governance, the discipline boundary through discipline-governance, and the first exercise through the Governance bounded-context owner.
